title: Transfer round-up: Sevilla get Everton’s Sandro and Swansea’s Mesa on loan
trail: Everton’s Sandro Ramírez and Swansea’s Roque Mesa have joined Sevilla on loan while Manchester City have signed Jack Harrison for £4m and immediately loaned him to Middlesbrough
body: Everton’s striker Sandro Ramírez has returned to Spain only six months into his Premier League career after joining Sevilla on loan until the end of the season. The Spain Under-21 international arrived at Goodison Park for £5.2m in the summer after Everton activated the release clause in his contract with Málaga. Sandro had scored 16 goals in 32 games for Málaga last season and his transfer was viewed as a potential bargain but he has struggled to settle in the Premier League and will sign for Sevilla on Wednesday subject to a medical. The 22-year-old, a product of Barcelona’s academy system, started only three league games for Everton and made 15 appearances in total, scoring once. Sevilla will have an option to sign Sandro on a permanent basis at the end of the season for a fee of around €9m (£7.9m). Everton embarked on an expensive recruitment drive last year but their investments have yielded poor results overall. Another summer signing, the £23.6m Davy Klaassen, has been told to leave on loan by the manager, Sam Allardyce, and has interest from Napoli. Another player to join Sevilla on loan is Swansea’s Roque Mesa. The Spaniard has made 16 appearances for the Welsh side since his £11m summer switch from Las Palmas. The 28-year-old has not featured in the Premier League since being substituted at half-time in Carlos Carvalhal’s first game in charge, a 2-1 win at Watford. Sevilla have also signed the left-back Miguel Layún on loan from Porto. Manchester City have completed the £4m signing of the England Under-21s midfielder Jack Harrison from their sister club New York City and immediately loaned him to Middlesbrough. Harrison was born in Stoke but moved to the US at the age of 14 and attracted rave reviews for his performances for New York during the 2017 MLS campaign. “I’ve really enjoyed my time with New York City and I’d like to thank Patrick Vieira and his coaching staff for helping me to develop as a player,” Harrison said after becoming Tony Pulis’s first Boro signing. Athletic Bilbao have wasted no time in replacing Aymeric Laporte, spending £28m on the central defender Iñigo Martínez from Real Sociedad. The 26-year-old will be presented on Wednesday after moving between the two Basque clubs, with Martínez signing a contract until 2023 after Bilbao met his release clause. Elsewhere in Spain Real Betis have signed Marc Bartra from Borussia Dortmund for £9.2m. The 27-year-old played 51 times and scored five goals for the Bundesliga side following his move from Barcelona in 2016 but has struggled for minutes recently under Peter Stöger. As one La Masia graduate leaves Dortmund, another arrives with the highly rated attacking midfielder Sergio Gómez joining from Barcelona for £2.6m. Watford have announced they have signed the winger Dodi Lukebakio from the Belgian side Charleroi while Leicester have allowed the striker Ahmed Musa to rejoin CSKA Moscow on loan until the end of the season.
